cells.tense: You can sit with someone in what's hard and not lose yourself in it.
cells.ask: Send one person a short message about what you're walking into, and let it go without carrying the thread further.
cells.core:
You can feel what someone else is carrying and stay yourself while you do it. That's not common. Most people either harden up when it gets heavy or get pulled under, and you're neither. The room doesn't have to be fixed, and you don't have to take it on. That's the thing you're good at.

And when a connection is thinning, you can see it. You don't cling to the shape of something that isn't working. You've made a decision that cost someone you cared about, and you still want to know what connects. Presence like yours gets spent holding people who have already left. Look at one bond you're keeping alive out of history rather than closeness, and say what you actually want there. Feed the thing that's real and let the rest go.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel with people and stay yourself.
cells.verb: walking toward what actually connects, and letting the rest stay behind
cells.place: in the company of people you can feel with and stay yourself

cells.tense: You're living past a goodbye that hasn't actually happened yet, bracing for a door you've already closed in your head.
cells.ask: Have one conversation where you ask something you don't already know about the other person, and let the answer stand without steering.
cells.core:
You're three moves ahead, and the person in front of you hasn't arrived yet. You've already stepped through a door they don't know you found, already written how this ends, and you're steering to match a picture that isn't real. Say it plainly and people hear a verdict.

Here's what runs under it: what if they don't stay, what if this slips. So you hold tighter, decide faster, make clear what it means. All that holding is taking a toll on the connection itself. You don't need to feel less. You need one structure you can't argue with — a fixed time, one honest sentence — and then the not-knowing has a home. Let them be actual in the room.
cells.sheetLine: You're already leaving, and nobody else has moved.
cells.verb: walking toward what actually connects, and letting the rest stay behind
cells.place: in the company of people you can feel with and stay yourself

cells.tense: You were the one who left, and part of you is still back at that threshold, watching it from a distance.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you know about staying close, then tell one person something true about your own week that you'd normally keep.
cells.core:
You stepped away from a bond, and the step is done. Part of your attention is at the door, going over it, so you're not quite in the room you're already in. Half of you is elsewhere.

Getting close seems to come with a price, and so you've held back the part of you that feels with people. That's a real loss, and it's costing you friendships now. What's absent isn't feeling. It's one clear picture of when you started keeping your care out of the room, and what that keeping protected. Put the pattern in front of you plainly. Then rejoin the room you're actually standing in. The connection is still there to pick up.
cells.sheetLine: You left that bond and you're still at the door.
cells.verb: walking toward what actually connects, and letting the rest stay behind
cells.place: in the company of people you can feel with and stay yourself

cells.tense: The choices about who you keep near are being made by you, and you talk as if they were just how things shook out.
cells.ask: Name one bond you'd call fragile or difficult, note down what you've already put into it, then tell that person one true thing you want from it.
cells.core:
You'd say you're someone who's along for the ride, going with the flow of who happens to be nearby. But you're not. Which connections get your time, which calls you return, who you let in close — those calls are being made right now, quietly, and they're yours.

There's something steady underneath how you move through people, a way of holding your own shape while you stay close. You've kept it careful and called it normal. Your part in this didn't start recently. The question is what to do with it, not whether it's there. Own one choice you've made about a bond and see what that starts.
cells.sheetLine: The choosing is yours, not the drift.
